agents_spawned.task_context: Refine issue #1059: Implement overseer agent for pipeline health monitoring. The issue has detailed requirements including: tiered Haiku/Opus architecture, adaptive stall detection, HITL-only restart authority, always-on auto-spawn, and integration with shared/egg_agent/. Your job: review the requirements for completeness, identify gaps or ambiguities, ensure the infrastructure changes list is complete, validate the design decisions, and produce a refined requirements document in .egg-state/drafts/. Key areas to validate: (1) How does the overseer container get spawned alongside coordinator — what changes to container_spawner.py are needed? (2) Are the file access patterns for overseer role complete? (3) Is the CLAUDE.md overseer section scope well-defined? (4) Check dependency status of #1088 (Agent SDK) and #1027 (message bus). (5) Validate the overseer vs mediator boundary is clear.

Review the refinement of issue #1059: Implement overseer agent for pipeline health monitoring. This is a large feature adding a new always-on monitoring agent to the SDLC pipeline. Review the requirements for: completeness of infrastructure changes, clarity of the tiered Haiku/Opus architecture, whether the overseer role restrictions match coordinator patterns, whether the adaptive stall detection approach is sound, and whether the HITL escalation ladder is well-defined. Flag any gaps, contradictions, or missing edge cases.

Review the agent design for issue #1059: Implement overseer agent for pipeline health monitoring. Focus on: (1) Is the tiered Haiku/Opus architecture appropriate — are the responsibilities well-split between tiers? (2) Is the monitoring loop design efficient — poll intervals, caching, budget constraints? (3) Is the self-monitoring design sufficient — can the overseer actually detect its own malfunctions? (4) Is the escalation flow clear and complete — nudge → redirect → HITL → issue → Slack? (5) Does the overseer vs mediator boundary handle all edge cases? (6) Are the CLAUDE.md prompt instructions comprehensive enough for an autonomous overseer? (7) Is the always-on spawn approach correct — should it be opt-in instead?

Design: (1) Overseer module structure under a new directory (e.g., overseer/ or within orchestrator/), (2) Tiered Haiku/Opus architecture using shared/egg_agent/ for all LLM calls, (3) Monitoring loop with adaptive stall detection, (4) Integration points with orchestrator (auto-spawn, container_spawner.py changes), (5) New AgentRole enum value and FileAccessPattern, (6) CLAUDE.md overseer section, (7) PipelineConfig additions. Write the architecture plan to .egg-state/drafts/. Dependencies #1027 (message bus), #1028 (coordinator), #1088 (Agent SDK) are all merged.

Create a detailed task breakdown for issue #1059: Implement overseer agent for pipeline health monitoring. Read the issue (gh issue view 1059) and refine outputs in .egg-state/agent-outputs/. Break down into ordered implementation tasks with clear acceptance criteria. Key areas: (1) Add OVERSEER role to AgentRole enums and role definitions, (2) Add overseer config to PipelineConfig, (3) Modify container_spawner.py for overseer spawning, (4) Auto-spawn logic in pipelines.py, (5) Exclude from coordinator_max_agents in coordinator.py, (6) Core overseer monitoring loop, (7) Haiku monitor agents (stall, loop, error, off-track detection), (8) Opus decision-maker integration, (9) Corrective action system (nudge/redirect/HITL/issue/Slack), (10) Self-monitoring, (11) CLAUDE.md overseer section, (12) Oversight logging to .egg-state/oversight/. Write tasks to .egg-state/drafts/.

Analyze risks for issue #1059: Implement overseer agent for pipeline health monitoring. Read the issue (gh issue view 1059) and refine outputs in .egg-state/agent-outputs/. Key risks to assess: (1) Overseer token cost — Haiku/Opus calls could be expensive if anomaly detection triggers too frequently, (2) Overseer itself becoming a bottleneck or failure point, (3) False positive stall detection disrupting healthy agents, (4) Circular monitoring — overseer watching coordinator watching overseer, (5) Race conditions with auto-spawn alongside coordinator, (6) Impact on container resource limits, (7) Edge cases in overseer vs mediator boundary, (8) Dependency on shared/egg_agent/ package stability. Write risk analysis to .egg-state/drafts/.

Review the architecture and task plans for issue #1059: Implement overseer agent for pipeline health monitoring. Wait for architect and task_planner outputs in .egg-state/drafts/, then review for: (1) Architecture completeness — does it cover all infrastructure changes listed in the issue? (2) Task ordering — are dependencies between tasks correct? (3) Risk mitigation — are the identified risks adequately addressed? (4) Feasibility — can this be implemented in a single PR or should it be split? (5) Missing pieces — any requirements from the issue not covered in the plan? Write review to .egg-state/agent-outputs/.

Implement issue #1059: Overseer agent for pipeline health monitoring. Read the architecture plan and task breakdown in .egg-state/drafts/ and the issue (gh issue view 1059). Implementation tasks in priority order:

1. Add OVERSEER to AgentRole enum in orchestrator/models.py
2. Add OVERSEER role definition with AgentRoleDefinition and FileAccessPattern in shared/egg_contracts/agent_roles.py — no repo access (same as coordinator pattern)
3. Add overseer config fields to PipelineConfig in orchestrator/models.py (overseer_enabled, overseer_poll_interval_seconds, overseer_stall_base_threshold_seconds, overseer_max_redirects_before_escalation)
4. Modify orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py to auto-spawn overseer alongside coordinator
5. Modify orchestrator/routes/coordinator.py to exclude overseer from coordinator_max_agents guardrail
6. Update container_spawner.py to support overseer with appropriate env vars (EGG_AGENT_ROLE=overseer, EGG_OVERSEER_MODE=true, no repo mount)
7. Create the overseer module (e.g., overseer/ directory) with:
   - Core monitoring loop (poll cycle, container status, heartbeats, message bus)
   - Haiku monitor agents using shared/egg_agent/ (stall classification, loop detection, error triage, off-track detection)
   - Opus decision-maker using shared/egg_agent/ (corrective action decisions)
   - Adaptive stall detection with configurable thresholds
   - Corrective action ladder (nudge → redirect → HITL → issue filing → Slack)
   - Self-monitoring (own cycle timing, message volume, LLM call budget)
   - Oversight logging to .egg-state/oversight/
   - Pipeline health summary at completion
   - Autonomous issue filing with structured diagnostic template and overseer-alert label
8. Add CLAUDE.md overseer agent prompt section (similar to Coordinator Agent section)

Use shared/egg_agent/ (run_agent_async) for ALL LLM calls. No direct Claude API calls. Check prior agent outputs in .egg-state/agent-outputs/ and .egg-state/drafts/ for architecture decisions.
